x: Three new names are appearing regularly in recent results---Bob Picton (20) Mike Hamlin (20) and Chas Capener (19). Jack Goswell is enthusiastic about their potential and considers that with Gerry Cameron (still only 20) we have a quartet worth watching.

In the 'D' section Mick Hamlin and Bob Picton two of our young members who are showing plenty of improvement won their 6 mile badges. In section 'C' we saw some fine walking from Steve Laker-Jones when he finished 2nd and covered 7mls 196yds thus winning his 7 mile Badge.
New member Gerald Johnson did well to finish 81st in 65:19. Pat Duncan, Charlie Capener and Bob Picton are now beginning to move thro' the fields and faster times are in store.
Gerry Cameron won the "Horwood Cup" for the 1965 Club Junior '7'. His time of 61:53 was 49 seconds better than runner-up Bob Picton, but Bob got his revenge in the handicap by taking first prize.

Eric Hall was a comfortable winner in a very good time, and Bob Barnes showed a welcome return to form in finishing 5th. Steven Laker-Jones was another to perform well and Bob Picton did extremely well in this, his first 'ten'.
Bob Picton in his second '10' found the going hard and had to give in at 8 miles. The remainder went well but were too far back to make any impression on the team leaders.

Ted Smith soon followed in 8th place and then everything depended on the positioning of Wishart (SWC) and Bob Picton. Unfortunately the Surrey man got home just 10secs ahead of Bob and this enabled his club to tie the match.

Further back Keown was moving along well, ahead of Bob Picton and Bernard Eglinton. Our two soigneurs Ray Hall and Harry Shields performed noble feats of endurance with the sponge and bottle and by the start of the third lap Belgrave looked well placed although Bob was forced to retire.

In the Southern Counties Track '7' both Bob Picton and Brian Ward broke 60 Minutes to win their '7' in the hour badges. Ray Hall is on the trail back to fitness again, giving Carl Lawton a close shave in the SCAAA six at Battersea the other week.

Our lads all excelled themselves in this first track race, Len Duquemin and John Moullin achieving first class standard and therefore their Club Honours Badges, Brian Ward and Bob Picton breaking the hour.

In the five Ray Middleton scored a resounding win over Don Thompson with Carl Lawton and Bob Picton backing up very well. Len Duquemin proceeded to repeat Rays example in the three and only six seconds prevented John Moullin from doing the same over two.

Doug Fotheringham, Bob Picton and Bob Coates all walked well to put Belgrave amongst the medals for the second year running. The spotlight however was on the superlative display of Wil Wesch who thrashed a much fancied Dave Watson to take the individual honours.
Brian Ward, Gerry Cameron and Bob Picton all looked to be on the trail again and up north Dave King and Paul Duckett are sure to be slipping in some crafty sessions.
Barry Ingarfield confirmed his recent form with Doug Fotheringham and Bob Picton both supporting well. Newcomer from Ireland John Johnson failed to break 100 minutes but scored in the team.

There is considerable disquiet about the standard of judging and this was just another case where the system has been brought into disrepute at the expense of an individual athlete. Bob Picton took advantage of a favourable section to finish third in a useful time/distance ratio.
Some safe walking from Barry Ingarfield and strong backing in the shape of John Bromley Doug Fotheringham and Bob Picton gave Belgrave an unexpected 2nd place in this 'Junior' championship.
Bernard Eglington made the long trip down from North Wales for the Belgrave Open '7'. Bob Picton showed just a little of what he could so easily be capable of in the Met.
He was almost caught by Dave McMullen and Ray Hall. Bob Picton it seems is getting less fat and more fit, maybe he is aiming to do well in the 'Garnet'.

John Hall was with the leading pack for the first four miles despite a heavy cold, and he gallantly held on for 7th position with the race being won by K.Emsley of Steyning. Bob Picton was our second man home with Doug Fotheringham and Eric Stroud, in only his second race for the Club, behind him.

John Hall placed 31st with John Dunsford and Dave McMullen well up. Ray Hall was forced to retire but Bob Picton and John Keown completed the distance. Waving the lantern rouge for Bels was Pat Duncan.

By 17 miles Carl had got back up to 4th with Len Duquemin 5th, however, at this point he tired drastically and recorded 24 minutes for the last 2 miles to finish 11th. John Dunsford was our fifth man with John Bromley and Bob Picton walking the last few miles together.

Even Bob Picton has made his reappearance as has Len Evans, in spectator capacity, after an operation. Richard Tanner and Alan Lucas have both been consistant performers over the last few months and it is with regret that Alan has now returned to Australia.

He walked his best race in our colours and with a little more class racing he could develop into a good walker. These four received their first championship medals for second team and they were ably supported by Bob Picton making a comeback.
John Dunsford followed and then John Hall (at last) dipped under 3 hours. P.B's were also produced by Bob Picton and Ron Day. In spite of all this we could only finish 5th team.

In 36½ place came the other two Johnnies, inside second class standard (try telling either of them that the other was 36th!) Our other two starters John Hall and Bob Picton unfortunately were among the non-finishers.
The winter season has slowly churned out some very good performances from some of the second string team, with Bob Picton showing the form that has been missing for a few seasons.

With only five starters we were not in the best of spirits but disaster followed and only two Belgravians finished. Bob Picton walked one of his best ever races for 9th in 84:02 and Ron Day 18th in 85:54.

This was another best forgotten National, once again due to unavoidable absenteeism - Bob Picton had put his hand through a window. Carl finished 4th and Ray Middleton backed up with Ron Day and Doug.
Carl Lawton led the boys home in 2nd position with Ray Middleton 18th. Bob Picton finally showed that perseverance pays off, in this case with a National medal to take home.

Ron Day, Dave King, John Morris, John Keown and Bob Picton saw to it that Belgrave retained that London to Brighton trophy. Ron became Belgrave champion at his first attempt at this 54 mile race and did particularly well on his melons and accolade.
A little way down the road at about 15 miles Dave King and Ron Day were together and later on came John Morris, John Keown and Bob Picton, all going well.

Bob Picton, still going with renewed vigour, has been throwing in some P.B.s and looks set for a good summer season. A run down on the last year's scoring teams shows that a remarkable number of no less than 19 walkers were involved.

Hot on his heels came Bob Picton, back in form again. With Enfield claiming second team medals the bronze medals seemed anybody's guess until the positions were added up.

Completing our quartet Bob Picton, who had shadowed Dave for many laps, began to drop away and had a real struggle over the last few laps. In common with other competitors our lads looked greatly relieved as they crossed the line for the last time.
There is always a team placed to be filled - Bob Picton at Highgate, Jon Dunsford at Luton, Richard Dorman (in his first outing as a team member) at Imber Court.

He was closely followed by Derek Howie, walking as an individual, with John Hall taking 3rd place in the Club Championship. Carl Lawton and Bob Picton completed the team. 1978 will not go down as a good year for us regarding the Championships.

These performances would not have been possible without help on the road by others so a tribute to the selfless efforts of Charlie McLennan, Jack Goswell, Bob Barnes, Gerry Cameron, Bob Picton, Carl Lawton and Pat Duncan, and when not competing against him, John Morris.
